proposals.title: Where your points went: points per miss by cause, a route-cliff line and a live what-if
proposals.what: SERVER: results gains `points`. For each miss i, gain_i = the section midpoint with only i flipped to the key, minus the actual midpoint. It re-runs scoring.score + section_score on the same route: 44 pure calls, a few ms. For a lower route it adds route_gap {m1_right, needed: 14 of 22 (ROUTE_UP_AT 0.6), short_by, cap: 580}, and gains past the cap read 0 with capped:true. Each miss gets one cause, the first rule that matches, derived when the report is read and never stored: TIME (blank, not reached, or answered in the module's last 10% of the clock in under 30 s); SLIP (right on Second look (proposal 3); before a second look, 'likely slip' = easy or medium, under 45 s, and a measured level of 3 or lower when one exists); TRAP (the pick names a misconception); GAP (the rest: an unnamed grid-in miss, or still wrong on second look). New POST /api/session/{sid}/whatif {flip:[qid]} returns {estimate, capped}. Module 2 is never re-routed, and the reply says so. HERO: under the gauge, one stacked bar 'Lost about 180 points' in four labelled segments, e.g. Time 40 (3) · Slips 55 (5) · Traps 65 (4) · Gaps 20 (1). Clicking a segment sets the review filter cause=<x> and scrolls to it. Helper: 'Points on the band's midpoint, using this report's own scoring (easy 1, medium 2, hard 3).' Route-cliff line, when route=lower and short_by ≤ 3: '1 more right in Module 1 would have earned the harder Module 2 and lifted the 580 cap. Your easiest Module 1 misses: M1 Q3 · M1 Q9', each chip opening the player. EVERYWHERE: every miss shows its gain ('≈ +19 pts') in the grid tooltip, the mistakes row, a 'Worth' table column (sortable) and the player header. WHAT-IF MODE: a toolbar toggle 'What if…'. While it is on, clicking a miss cell marks it with a ghost ✓, and the gauge redraws after a 150 ms debounce. Presets: 'Flip my slips' · 'Flip easy misses' · 'Flip time losses' · Reset. The spec's single whatif sentence becomes the 'Flip easy misses' preset.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep shows one score, counts, and a domainScore their UI never prints. Nothing says what each miss cost or why it was lost, and they cannot: their payload has no time, no skill and no misconception per option. Adaptive routing, the most misunderstood part of the digital SAT, is never explained. Ours turns a report into a price list of recoverable points.
proposals.needs: scoring.py stays pure and reusable (F4). Per-question ms from qstate (R7, S5 runner) for the TIME cause. Proposal 3 for confirmed slips. drill.levels() measured level (Practice §levels) is optional. UI.gauge redraw hook (F1 charts.js). A cause filter in the review filter bar.

proposals.title: A living report: Prove it, recovered points and 'this section today'
proposals.what: RULE (one server function, used by results and history): a miss is Recovered when the student's latest clean answer (R8) on the same template, after the sitting finished, is right, and its trap is closed or has ≥ 2 clean rights since. It is Slipping when that latest clean answer is wrong. This is one query over the sitting's templates, sharing the `history` query. RESULTS gains recovery {recovered:[qid], slipping:[qid], open:[qid], points_recovered, points_open, now_estimate}. now_estimate re-runs scoring with the recovered misses flipped. HERO: a second ghost band on the gauge labelled 'Today ≈ 570–710', captioned 'Rescored with what you have proven since, on these same question types. Not a new test.' Chip: 'Recovered 9 of 13 · +50 pts · 4 still open (60 pts)'. ACTIONS: a split primary 'Prove it · 13' beside Fix these. Prove it starts Tests' custom test {source:'misses', from_session:sid}: fresh seeds of each missed template, 95 s each, no feedback until hand-in, cfg.parent=sid. When it finishes, its report links back ('Proven 9 of 13 → Section #7 rescored'), and the proven cells take the Fixed-since token (§2.3), now driven by proof and not only by a trap closing. TIMELINE under the hero, from attempts and traps: 'Sep 23 sat · Sep 24 fixed 5 · Sep 26 proved 4 of 6 · Oct 1 slipped 1'. OVERVIEW: each sitting card gets a recovery ring 'Recovered 9/13'. Its wrong chips turn to a ✓ badge when recovered. The sittings sort gains 'Most points still open'. /api/history items add points_open, so Today can say 'Section #7 has 60 points still open'.
proposals.beats: Their report is a static photo of one day. Proving a fix needs a new question of the same type, and their finite papers can only re-show an item whose key the student has already seen, which tests memory. Nothing on their site shows that past mistakes have been dealt with.
proposals.needs: R8 clean answers and repeat filtering (F4), traps with closed/owed (R9), Tests' custom test from misses (S5, §3.4 custom queue), cfg.parent on child sittings (R24/F5), the Fixed-since status token (F1), and points from proposal 1.

proposals.title: Second look before the answers: tells a slip from a gap, then a fresh twin
proposals.what: TRIGGER: a finished mock, module or diagnostic with misses whose answers have not been viewed. A banner above the hero: 'Second look · 13 misses · answers still hidden · about 12 min' [Start second look] [Show answers]. UI.review MODE 'second': only the misses, in order. The key, the reasons, the explanation and the status are hidden. Your first pick shows struck, labelled 'Your first answer', and cannot be picked. Blanks can be answered, and grid-ins take a new entry. A per-question clock runs. FILING: each answer is filed as a repeat (R8: no mastery, closes nothing) and stored in qstate[qid].second = {answer, correct, ms} through POST /api/session/{sid}/state. KEEPING IT CLEAN: qstate[qid].seen_key is set the first time UI.review shows that question with answers visible. Those questions are left out, and the banner says '11 of 13 still unseen'. END SUMMARY: 'Right on a second look 5 → slips (you knew it) · Same answer again 4 · A different wrong answer 2 (a second trap) · Still blank 2'. Next rung: [Fresh twin of the 8 still wrong], a twin drill (source twin, each 1) played inline. Then: 'Right on a twin 3 → it clicked once you looked again · Wrong on a twin 5 → learn it', with 'Practise this skill' per row. The results feed proposal 1 (confirmed slips), a 'Second look' table column (✓/✕/–), the history rows and the player tag 'Right on a second look'.
proposals.beats: Their Hide answers cannot re-answer at all. Our spec's hidden-mode pick files nothing, so the evidence is thrown away. Nobody tells a careless miss from a real gap, and a real gap from 'learned it once shown'. The twin rung is impossible with a finite bank.
proposals.needs: qstate JSON gains second and seen_key (R7 column, F4; no new column). The UI.review 'second' mode (F3). The twin drill source (F5, R24). R8 repeat filing. It resolves the conflict with R21, where review re-answers file a repeat.

proposals.title: Best value next: points per minute for each skill, a forecast, and one tap to plan it
proposals.what: SERVER: `gains` per topic. results covers this sitting; /api/stats covers the mean over the last 3 scored sittings. Each topic has {points_lost (the sum of proposal 1's gains for its misses), open_traps, fix_rate (the share of this learner's traps in the topic closed within 7 days, falling back to the site-wide rate), minutes_to_fix (median clean answers to close a trap × this learner's average ms in the topic), value = points_lost × fix_rate ÷ minutes_to_fix}. REPORT section 'Best value next', after Mistakes, and an OVERVIEW card beside the estimate. Rows are sorted by value. Each row: the topic glyph and name · '≈ +25 pts a section' · '3 open mistakes · about 18 min' · a value bar · [Fix these 3] (drill {mistakes:true, topics:[slug]}) · a quiet 'Practise skill'. FORECAST line: 'Fix the top 3: about 590–730, and your target 700 falls inside it'. It re-runs scoring on the latest section with those topics' misses flipped, weighted by fix_rate and rounded to 10. A time line: 'At your 40 min a day (prefs.minutes), that is about 2 study days before Oct 3.' When a plan exists, [Add to plan] puts one fix task per top-3 skill on the next study days through Plan's task API, and the row then reads 'In your plan · Thu'. Helper: 'From this site's scoring and your own fix speed. It is a guide to order, not a promise.'
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's plan weights weak areas from what the student says, and their generator failed 3 times out of 3. Their report never prices a skill or estimates the time to fix it. Ours ranks by points actually lost and by the student's own measured fix speed, which needs per-question weights, named traps and fresh items.
proposals.needs: Proposal 1's gains. Trap open/close timestamps (R9, F4). prefs.minutes and exam_date (R11/R15). Plan task create/patch (S7, R14). /api/stats (S6). estimate.py for the target and band (R16).

proposals.title: Your trap pattern across question types, with a trap drill
proposals.what: The report gains a 'Trap pattern' section above Mistakes when some normalised misconception (the R9 `norm`) has ≥ 2 hits in this sitting or ≥ 3 all time. It groups misses across templates and topics. Each row shows: the concrete label; 'Changed the sign of the slope ×3 · in Linear functions, Systems, Lines (3 question types)'; the question refs as chips; 'also in 4 question types you haven't met' (from a bank index); and [Trap drill · 10]. TRAP DRILL: fresh MC items from any template whose options contain that norm, found by a seed walk (Review's spot and 'Practise across all' engine), with instant feedback. A right answer on an item that offered the trap counts as a clean answer toward every open trap with that norm. THE OVERVIEW's 'Top misconceptions' (spec 2.8) groups by norm across templates, not by template, and shows 'in 3 question types'. BANK INDEX: template → set of norms, built once by surveying seeds (as blueprint.survey does) and cached to a JSON file. PHASE 2: a curated map of about 20 families over the norms (sign, reciprocal, half/double, wrong base for a percent, wrong axis, radius/diameter, units), so the panel can say 'Sign errors ×5 across 4 skills'.
proposals.beats: Their 'Distractor Analysis' is prose inside one item. Nothing links one mistake to another, so they cannot say 'you keep doing this'. A finite bank cannot produce 10 new questions that all contain the same trap.
proposals.needs: attempts.norm and traps.norm (R8/R9, F4). The template→norms index (T-bank or F4). Review's cross-template drill and spot engine (S10), exposed as drill pool 'norm' (F5, §2.6). The family map is content work, later.

proposals.title: How well you judged yourself: confidence, flags, changes and time away
proposals.what: A report section 'Judgement' for tests, and for drills with confidence tags on. It consumes data the Tests runner already sends but the report spec never shows. (1) A 3×2 matrix, Sure / Unsure / Guess × Right / Wrong, with counts, each cell a filter. 'Sure and wrong · 3: the most urgent. You believed these traps', listing each named misconception with [Fix]. 'Guessed and right · 2: counted, but not learned; added to Review as Unsure' (R9 kind unsure). (2) Flags: 'Flagged 5 · went back to 4 · changed 2, both wrong → right · 1 flagged and left wrong'. An advice line picked by rule: flags that paid off → 'Keep flagging and coming back'; flags never revisited ≥ 2 → 'Leave 3 minutes at the end for your flags'. (3) Answer changes (spec 1.10 moves here) with all-time first-instinct data: 'When you change an answer you end up right 62% of the time (21 changes)'. (4) Away: 'Left the test window 3 times · 2:10' from qstate._session. Empty state with tags off: 'Turn on confidence tags in test settings to see how well you judge your answers', with the toggle (prefs).
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep counts flags and nothing more: no confidence, no change trail, no away time. Only a bank whose distractors are labelled can name the misconception a student was sure of. Tests §3.4.4 promises this calibration 'in the report', and the report spec never shows it.
proposals.needs: qstate conf, trail, first, changes and _session away_ms/away_n (R7; the S5 runner sends them). prefs.confidence (R11). The traps 'unsure' kind (R9). The flags table (R5).

proposals.title: Pace map and speed sets built from your slow question types
proposals.what: Replaces spec 1.9. (a) A per-question dot plot: x = question order with a gap between M1 and M2, y = seconds, each dot drawn in its status glyph. Each question has a short reference tick at the median time other students take on that template (n ≥ 20, else 95 s). (b) Under it, a cumulative-clock line per module against the even-pace line, annotated 'fell behind at M2 Q14' and 'blanks start here'. Four quadrant chips, each a filter with a count: Banked (right, under the median), Time sink (right, over 1.5× the median), Rushed (wrong, under 0.5× the median), Stuck (wrong, over 1.5× the median). Line: 'Time sinks cost 6:20. At median pace you would have reached your 2 blanks.' [Speed set · 8]: fresh twins of the time-sink types, each timed at that type's median, with instant feedback. Its summary shows your time against the target per question. [Careful set · 3]: the rushed-miss types, untimed, with a confirm-before-submit step. Phone: the dot plot scales to 358px and the clock line stacks under it.
proposals.beats: Their report has no time per question at all. Their only time analysis is an empty contest chart of average seconds by difficulty. A speed set on the same question type with new numbers needs an unlimited bank, and a per-type time benchmark needs every answer recorded.
proposals.needs: qstate ms (R7, S5). A per-template median ms aggregate over attempts.ms, cached with drill.levels() crowd stats (Practice §levels). A per-question target time in the drill body (F5, §2.6 timing) and the practice session (S4). UI.barChart or a dot variant (F1 charts.js).

proposals.title: Then vs now: question-by-question comparison of parallel sittings
proposals.what: When a sitting was built as a parallel form (Tests' kind 'twin' twin_of, or the report's 'Retake as a test'), the report gains a 'Compared with Section #6' section. There is one row per slot (M1 Q1…M2 Q22): skill, difficulty, the then and now status cells, and time then → now. Summary chips, each a filter: Improved 8 (✕→✓) · Held 27 · Slipped 2 (✓→✕) · Still missing 5. Slipped rows come first, since they are the surprise. The header delta is explained: '+60: 8 improved (+95 pts), 2 slipped (−35)', using proposal 1's gains. For a sitting that is not parallel, a 'Compare with…' picker lists earlier sittings and compares on shared templates only ('19 question types appear in both'). Opening a row opens UI.review in a two-up mode with both versions side by side: same type, different numbers, your two answers.
proposals.beats: Their papers are different fixed forms, so nothing can be compared item by item, and resitting the same paper measures memory. 'Did I actually get better at these question types?' is only answerable with parallel forms on demand.
proposals.needs: One parallel-form contract: use Tests' POST /api/mock/new {kind:'twin', twin_of} and drop the report's duplicate {like}. A slot map stored in cfg (S5). A results `compare` field (S6). A UI.review two-up mode (F3).

proposals.title: Measured difficulty and 'should-have-had' misses
proposals.what: For each template: the share right on first clean attempts across all learners, and the measured level 1–7, both from drill.levels() (the Practice spec's single function, n ≥ 20). Shown in: the player header ('Level 3 · 81% of students get this type right'); Details ('measured from 212' or 'not measured yet · 8 so far'); a table column; and a 'Colour by: Level' grid view that uses the §2.3 tints with the level number. Filter chips: 'Should-have-had · 4' (misses on types that ≥ 75% of students get right) and 'Hard wins · 3' (rights on types under 35%). Hero line: '4 of your misses are on types most students get right: the cheapest points in this report.' Below n = 20 only the College Board tier shows, never a guessed level.
proposals.beats: Their Details show a fixed Easy/Medium/Hard label. Their Question Score 1–7 is only a builder filter, is opaque, and appears on no report. Ours is measured from real first tries and says how many it is measured from.
proposals.needs: drill.levels() and its crowd rate (Practice §3.3.5, cached 10 min). First-clean-attempt filtering (R8). Filter bar chips (F1).

proposals.title: Question-type coverage map on /results/
proposals.what: A section 'Question types · 185 of 386 met · 142 proven', 19 skill rows grouped by domain. Each row has one small cell per template: not met (outline), met (tile), open mistake (orange dot), proven (orange fill: the last 2 clean answers right), slipping (graphite, last clean answer wrong). Each state has a glyph and a legend with counts. Hover or tap shows the type name, measured level, 'your record 4/5 · last Sep 22' and [5 like this]. Clicking starts a 5-question twin set of that type. Controls: Show all / not met / open / proven, and [Practise 10 types you haven't met] (drill pool 'untried'). The Questions tile's sub-line gains 'types met 185/386'. Phone: cells wrap at 12px with 44px hit areas through row-level tap targets that open a sheet listing that skill's types.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep counts questions solved out of a finite pool (1,921 Math), which says nothing about what has been covered. We can show the whole space of question types the SAT samples, and fill any gap on demand.
proposals.needs: /api/bank types (Practice, 386 templates with names). A per-template attempts aggregate for the learner (F4). Drill pools 'untried' and types (F5). The share view must honour ?share= (R18).

proposals.title: Instant key checker on reports, and automatic rescoring when a question is fixed
proposals.what: CHECKER: in UI.report, the categories 'Wrong answer key', 'Two answers are right' and 'No right answer' call POST /api/report/check {session, question_id}. The server regenerates the item from (template, seed), runs satbank audit (the independent re-derivation every shipped item already passes), and checks numerically that no distractor equals the key. Within a second the dialog shows: 'Our checker re-derived the key independently: D (73 ≤ t ≤ 111). Each other option comes from a named mistake: A …, B …, C …', then [Send anyway]. A failed check marks the report high priority for admins. RESCORE: when an admin resolves a report as 'key fixed' (the template changed), a job regenerates every stored (template, seed) in finished sittings. If the stem and choices are unchanged, the stored answer is re-marked against the new key. If the item changed, the question is voided (the ⊘ token, left out of scoring). Attempts and traps are corrected. Affected reports show a strip: 'M1 Q7 was corrected on Oct 2 after a report. This sitting was rescored: 520–660 → 530–670.' The reporter sees 'Your report fixed this question type for every future student' in Settings › Your reports. Old grid-in misses are renamed the same way when a template gains spr_mistakes.
proposals.beats: Their report modal sends an exam ID into silence, and a fixed paper cannot correct past scores. Every one of our items is re-derivable and addressed exactly, so the fix reaches every past sitting and the student hears about it.
proposals.needs: The F6 report system and admin (R17). satbank audit callable at runtime. A template version tag in the bank (T-bank). A rescore job over sessions.questions (F4/S6). The Voided token (F1). spr_mistakes (T-bank, open question 11) for renaming grid-ins.

proposals.title: Repair pack: the report printed with fresh practice and a key
proposals.what: The ⋯ menu gains 'Print repair pack', which also works on a shared read-only link so a tutor or parent can print it. Page 1: the hero, points by cause and Best value next. Then, per miss: the original question regenerated exactly, your answer, the key, the misconception and the explanation. Then 'Fresh practice': 1–3 twins per miss (a select, default 2) with space to work. Last page: the key, with every option's misconception. Print CSS only, with page breaks never splitting a question. The seeds are remembered as seen. Footer: 'These answers are not filed. Enter them online: <short link>', which opens the pack as an end-mode practice set that files answers and can close traps.
proposals.beats: Their 'Share / Export Report' button has no handler. A printed paper from a finite bank is the same paper every time, while ours is new every print and targets exactly this sitting's traps.
proposals.needs: Review's GET /api/review/worksheet (S10), called with ids from the session. The R19 access() rule. Print conventions in ui.css (F1). Share tokens (R18) for the tutor path.

parity_gaps.feature: Accuracy and time by difficulty and format
parity_gaps.spec_says: Easy/Medium/Hard and MC/Grid-in rows: right/answered, %, a bar and average time.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their contest Time Analysis ('average seconds per answered question, by difficulty'), moved to every sitting.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Benchmark each row and each question against other students' median time on the same templates and against the 95 s pace. Add a 'Time sinks' list of slow-but-right types with a Speed set (proposal 7).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Questions, Accuracy, Study time, Tests, Streak, Mistakes.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their profile tiles (Streak / Tests / Solved / Vocab) with windows stated.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add 'Question types 185/386 met · 142 proven', a count only a type-addressed bank has, linking to the coverage map (proposal 10). Mistakes shows 'fixed this week' beside open.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Crowd from first attempts grouped by (template, seed) across the day's challenge sessions: 'A 12% · B 41% · C 9% · D 38%'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It matches their per-contest stats, and v2-decisions #1 (twin challenges: each student gets their own numbers) breaks it: no two students share a seed, so option letters never line up.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Group by template and by misconception norm: '41% right · "forgot to halve" 31% · "added base and height" 12%'. The same query then serves every question type in every report, not only challenges.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Kind, seq, date, time, minutes and Timed/Untimed.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their 'PRACTICE TEST REVIEW · Paper #47 · date', plus a sequence number.
parity_gaps.upgrade: State the conditions that affect the score's validity: 'Official timing · calculator on · paused 0 · away 0:40 · extended time off'. Add a badge 'Counts toward your estimate', or 'Practice only: paused twice / 1.5× time', from Tests' pause and extended-time data.
